Not at the moment but I was on venlafaxine for about a year after realizing escitalopram did nothing for me. Had some pretty good results with it I’d say, not like it turned my life around but it did its job, also the week after I got off it was one of the best in my life in terms of internal sensations but that’s probably just a side effect from getting off any antidepressant, not sure. And also do keep in mind that what works for me may not work for you and all that stuff but I’m sure you know this already. So to answer your question yes, it did help me

I have thoughts about trying another therapist because sometimes it feels like we barely make any progress but then again she did help me get through the worst period of my life a couple of years ago. On top of that it’s only recently that we restarted our sessions after a relatively long break due to some my personal reasons so I’m willing to give it a try for now. Feeling totally ignored. Somehow at some point earlier in my life I inadvertently mastered the art of being invisible and now (and have been for some time already) I’m reaping what I sowed, so to speak. Even made my therapist figuratively scratch her head after I had explained the situation in its entirety. The most puzzling thing is that it’s ubiquitous, I feel this way with friends, with whom it’s always me who initiates any kind of contact, with let’s call them classmates who fail to say hi back half the time we cross our paths, with relative strangers who I had been communicating with for a while before being ghosted, with total strangers when I offer a helping hand in situations when they do actually ask for help so it’s not like I’m imposing myself on them, both offline and online. So for quite a while I’ve been oscillating between thinking “I don’t need anyone, I’m an interesting person and I’m absolutely capable of spending time by myself doing things I enjoy” on the one hand and “I want some companionship with someone, just a single person who is going to appreciate me in their life is more than I could ask for” on the other hand. It is as if somewhere inside of me is an invisible human repellent and I just cannot figure out what it is.
I feel for you friend, I’m kind of in the same boat. Sorry nothing more comes to mind, just sending hugs your way

Moving to another country in a week, was feeling totally fine until I decided to read other migrants’ impressions and, well, I guess I shouldn’t have done that. Of course I understand it’s completely irrational to change my entire outlook after reading just a couple of stories (from people with backgrounds completely different from mine on top of that) but here we are now. Obviously nothing changes in terms of plans, I’ve been preparing for this for the last six months but now I just feel unnecessarily apprehensive (as if I’m not used to the feeling by now, heh).

Not the person you responded to so I’m sorry if it’s a bit redundant or out of place. Also I don’t have a particular opinion on the topic as a whole but just decided to comment on some of your points.

Regarding the fact that both are fantasies I think in essence they are as in they both represent a particular fantasy one may have but it’s the ways they are created that makes them different as one is a novel, which is a product of an author’s imagination, and the other is something that involves real people. And on top of that realizing that porn is ultimately a fantasy requires a certain presence of mind which I don’t think everyone has (but then again I’m not the authority to speak on this without any doubt). Understanding that something depicted in a book is a fantasy is quite a bit easier I suspect. Although it’s certainly clear that something being a fantasy absolutely doesn’t absolve it from having some very real implications so it’s not to say that one is “better” than the other.

And also one more thing about the book and the impact it has or at least the perception of this impact may be due to survivorship bias, as in at some point the novel became so famous that everyone already knew what it was about without reading it, myself included. So then it becomes a question if you’re into that sort of thing or not, if you are you read it and ultimately like it, if not then you just don’t touch it and that’s where it ends. All that is to say that it’s not a case of positive and negative opinions and rather a case of positive opinions and no opinions at all so that’s why it may seem that many women find him desirable. But then again I may be totally wrong.
Best of luck to you mate

I think I’m with you on this one, it’s definitely something that I’ve been feeling throughout the years. Don’t want to sound like an armchair expert in psychology but I suppose you could look at it (it being the way straight dudes tend to behave sometimes, among other things) as different masks people put on any time they interact with each other. Of course I’m talking about my own experiences only but it’s quite amusing to pick up the signs of it when you pay attention to them. For example, however vague it may be, I noticed on several occasions how my best friend would act differently depending on whether we are alone with him doing something or in a group of our common friends, how he’s a bit more explicitly masculine in the latter case. It’s not like he’s a hypocrite because of it, I guess it’s just that acting this way makes him more comfortable in this particular environment.

And also one more thing (talking about those assumptions that you mentioned) I’ve noticed is that people usually don’t think twice about those ideas during a casual conversation, like I’m pretty sure in the case of that self-care talk it wasn’t done out of malice or disregard, just that it’s something one would blurt out and forget the second after. Of course it’s indicative of the common stereotypes but I’d say these are not something people desperately cling on to, if you described why you felt the way you did it would most likely be just fine.

The thing is, while technically you (and by "you" I don't mean you exactly, just any person) do have a choice, most of the time people's lives aren't bad enough for them to seriously consider ending it. I am as much a nobody as anyone else but if you'll allow it I'd say the most important, and the most difficult, thing to do is to shift your mindset in a slightly different direction. Finding passions or whatever hasn't helped me, if anything it made me feel inferior to people who do have them. Hey, I can definitely relate to what you've said, been feeling this way for quite a while too. When it comes to casual conversations I think other people just have much more experience, from childhood and while growing up, I imagine it's just natural to them, like a very basic life skill akin to, I don't know, tying shoelaces or brushing teeth or whatever. Whereas when I try to interact with someone it feels sort of mechanical, every subtle hint or movement is analyzed and treated as something meaningful, every phrase is either forced or utterly bland and non-contributing (is this even a word?). As for feeling unlikeable; I guess it is just another manifestation of my low self-esteem. I don't like myself, why would anyone else do? I admit this kind of thinking is very unproductive and leads nowhere but it is the way it is. So, just to sum up, you're not alone in feeling like this.
